nodes.label: Original SRP design brief (weak-learner MLPs → attention)
nodes.rationale: MLPs deliberately kept to 1-2 layers and 4-16 neurons with weight penalties so each focuses on a few important features; the whole stack is trained end to end and the attention module produces the prediction. Must eventually be validated on large datasets, with small ones (wine, housing) only for visualising the idea.

nodes.label: Similarity-matrix diversity loss
nodes.rationale: Build an nxn similarity matrix over the MLPs' output feature vectors and penalise the mean off-diagonal, so the MLPs cannot all learn the same thing; more diversity was expected to mean more accuracy.

nodes.label: Cosine similarity diversity measure
nodes.rationale: Catches directional similarity between the weak learners' feature vectors; paired with Pearson because the two are complementary.

nodes.label: Pearson correlation diversity measure
nodes.rationale: Catches linear redundancy in what the MLPs learned, which cosine similarity alone misses; `combined` mode averages both.

nodes.label: [CLS] token aggregation
nodes.rationale: A learnable token appended last so that under the triu causal mask its row is all-zeros and it attends to every weak learner, making it the natural read-out point.

nodes.label: CLS-token removal alternatives (mean pool / last token / weighted sum)
nodes.rationale: Supervisor asked to drop the CLS token. Last-token read-out was argued most theoretically motivated because under causal attention token K has already attended to everything before it, mirroring boosting's last tree having the most context; mean pooling is simplest and treats all MLPs equally; weighted sum adds K learned softmaxed weights.

nodes.label: Causal mask as gradient-boosting analogy
nodes.rationale: Token i attends only to 0..i (torch.triu(..., diagonal=1) filled with -inf) so that whatever the first learner already captured, the second need not relearn — exactly the gradient-boosted-trees intuition the architecture is built on.

nodes.label: Diversity-weight ablation (sweet spot 0.05)
nodes.rationale: val_loss 0.2855 (w=0) → 0.2814 (w=0.05) → 0.3028/0.3058/0.3035 at 0.10/0.50/1.00. Negative final div values mean the optimizer pushed the MLPs past 'different' into anti-correlated, spending capacity on being opposite rather than useful — so diversity must act as a regularizer, not the primary objective.

nodes.label: Diversity-weight scheduling (warm-up vs annealing)
nodes.rationale: Warm-up (div_w = min(target, target*epoch/warmup_epochs)) is preferred over annealing because applying diversity pressure before the MLPs have learned anything leaves nothing useful to diversify — mirroring boosting, where diversity is a consequence of the sequential structure rather than forced from the start. Turns the ablation into a 2D grid of target weight x schedule type.
